display.title: Episode 118: The Needles and Toothpicks, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: Right after Purim, Uncle Yossi begins the parable of the needles and toothpicks: a king asks a rabbi why Hashem punishes Jews, but not other nations, for worshipping idols.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week after Purim 5744. Uncle Yossi looks back at the holiday: gifts to the poor, shalach manos that bind friends together in Ahavas Yisroel and achdus, and an invitation to write in about how listeners spent Purim. After the Hakochainik march and the sponsor, a six-year-old guest recites the Shema. Story time opens with the first two of the Ten Commandments, which forbid serving anyone but Hashem. A king who admires the Jewish people asks a rabbi why the Torah warns Jews so strictly against idols, while other nations switch from one idol to another without warning. The rabbi answers with a story. Reuven gives his son Shimon 2,000 gold coins to start a business, but a stranger talks Shimon into buying a trainload of toothpicks with no points. His patient father gives him a second chance, and Shimon comes home with needles that have no eyes. The chapter ends with a promise of a funny conclusion next week. The show closes with the Matzah Ball Race contest.
display.lesson: Hashem alone is to be served; the answer to the king's question comes in the next chapter.
